problem:
A quadratic equation in the variable $x$ with real coefficients has a root $x=\frac{7\text{i}}{5}.$ Given that the coefficient of ${x}^{2}$ in the equation is $25,$ find the equation. Write your answer in the form $a{x}^{2}+bx+c=0,$ where $a,$ $b,$ and $c$ are real constants.

{{field-1}}$=0$
worked_solution:
Since the quadratic equation has real coefficients and $x=\frac{7\text{i}}{5}$ is a root, its conjugate $x=-\frac{7\text{i}}{5}$ must also be a root. Therefore, using the zero product property, we can write a quadratic equation with the required roots as follows:

$$
(x-\frac{7\text{i}}{5})(x+\frac{7\text{i}}{5})=0
$$

Multiplying out the parentheses and simplifying gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-{(\frac{7\text{i}}{5})}^{2} & =0 \\ {x}^{2}-\frac{49}{25}(-1) & =0 \\ {x}^{2}+\frac{49}{25} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

This equation has roots $x=\pm \frac{7\text{i}}{5},$ but the coefficient of ${x}^{2}$ is not $25.$ Therefore, to find the desired equation, we multiply the equation above by $25.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}25({x}^{2}+\frac{49}{25}) & =0 \\ 25{x}^{2}+49 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
